title: FIRST BLOOM
logline: On a frozen blue-hour meadow, one frost-rimed bud bursts open. The spring it releases races across a snowbound mountain basin. It thaws a creek whose water reflects a sky that has not arrived yet, and it shatters a frozen waterfall into a double rainbow. From high above, the whole valley turns out to have bloomed into the same flower.

shots.name: 1 Rime
shots.camera: Shots 1-3 are one continuous macro take. 100 mm-equivalent macro about 6 cm from the bud, thin depth of field (f/2 look, about 1 cm in focus), slightly low angle so the bud stands against the pale horizon. Locked off with a slow 3% push-in and 0.2-degree micro-drift noise.
shots.content: Blue hour before sunrise. A single closed pasque-flower bud (six furled violet tepals sheathed in silky silver hairs, about 12 cm tall) stands out of a snowy meadow on a small knoll at the centre of the basin. Every hair is furred with rime, so the bud looks spun from frost. Frosted grass blades sit in soft foreground blur, the snow crust glitters as bokeh, and a few snowflakes drift slowly through focus. Background: a periwinkle snowfield and a lavender sky under a flat overcast deck, with one thin warm dawn slot on the horizon. The frame is almost monochrome; the only colour is deep violet showing in the seams between the frosted tepals. BUILD: parametric tepal mesh with shell/fin fuzz for the hairs, rime made of instanced ice-needle cards grown along the surface normals, analytic sky gradient, DOF.
shots.sound: Near silence: thin cold wind room tone, distant ice creaks, snow-crust ticks. Music: a single high string harmonic or glass tone fades in from 0.5s.

shots.name: 2 First Light
shots.camera: Same take. Rack focus from the foreground frost blades to the bud between 3.0s and 4.0s. The push-in continues to 6%.
shots.content: The sun clears the dawn slot. A blade of warm gold light slides across the snow from frame left, climbs the stem and wraps around the bud. Where it touches, the ice needles flare into star glints, turn glassy and bead into tiny dew drops. Snow sparkle ignites in the bokeh. With the light now behind it, the violet glows faintly through the hairs. BUILD: a 'melt' uniform travels with the light edge; it shrinks the rime cards and grows dew-sphere instances.
shots.sound: A slow, airy riser starts (bowed glass, breathy pad). Frost crackles and fizzes as the rime melts, with three tiny drip ticks at 4.2s, 4.7s and 5.0s. Music: a 3-4 note celesta or felt-piano motif enters; this motif returns at 27.5s.

shots.name: 3 Held Breath
shots.camera: Same take. The push-in stops dead and time ramps down to 30%, so the snowflakes almost hang in the air.
shots.content: Total stillness. The tepals strain apart by a hair, and a seam of hot gold light glows from inside the bud. One dew drop trembles at the tip. The frame holds.
shots.sound: The music drops to silence at 5.20s. All that remains is a soft reverse inhale swell, one low heartbeat-like thump at 5.60s and a tiny ice 'tink' at 5.85s.

shots.name: 4 First Bloom (HIT)
shots.camera: 6.00-6.70s: the macro holds as time snaps back to 100%, with a 4-frame impact shake of 1-2 px. 6.70-7.60s: a fast pull-back and lift at ground level (0.1 m to 6 m, eased), with the field of view widening from a 100 mm look to a 24 mm look, until the flower is a single violet spark in a vast snowfield.
shots.content: HIT at exactly 6.00s. In 10 frames the six tepals snap open with an overshoot wobble and fling their dew off in a sparkling spray. The backlit, translucent violet tepals glow around a crown of gold stamens, and a pulse of golden pollen and light blasts outward. During the pull-back the pulse becomes a low ring of gold light racing out across the snow. Behind it the snow turns to glitter mist and a ring of emerald grass spikes up around the flower. The overcast sky is still pale lavender. BUILD: the global wave clock starts here (T=0 at 6.00s). Close to the knoll an analytic radial distance blends into the baked arrival-time field.
shots.sound: HIT: a sub boom under the orchestral tutti downbeat. Layered on top: an organic petal-unfurl 'whoomp' (a cloth snap and a damp paper pop, pitched down), a crystalline burst shimmer, a dew-spray sparkle and an outward pollen whoosh. During the pull-back: an air whoosh and the rising sizzle of snow evaporating.

shots.name: 5 Wavefront
shots.camera: Cut. FPV at 18 mm, 1.2 m above the snow, flying east-southeast toward the low sun at about 30 m/s along the edge of a meltwater swale, banking up to 8 degrees either way with light rotational shake. The camera rides 3-6 m behind the front, so the line of transformation crosses the lower third of the frame. Accumulate 4-8 jittered sub-frames per frame on shots 5-8 for motion blur and to stop the grass shimmering.
shots.content: The front of spring runs ahead of us like a breaking wave: a band about 4 m wide where the snow flashes into sparkle mist, grass erupts to knee height in a springy ripple, and flowers pop open in staggered bursts, each with a puff of pollen. On the left, inside a petal lobe, are violet and cobalt flowers. A line of white daisies traces the lobe edge. On the right, poppy red-orange flowers dot emerald grass, with gold buttercups near the start. Ahead lies untouched, glittering snow crust and frosted shrubs; behind and under the lens, lush backlit colour. The sun is a soft disc behind thin overcast. Swallows burst up from the grass just ahead of the front and fly with us. BUILD: bloomMask = smoothstep(T - arrival(xz)). It drives the snow layer, grass scale (with overshoot) and flower opening, and it feeds a sparkle particle emitter at the front.
shots.sound: A driving ostinato enters (spiccato strings and pulse percussion). FPV air rush, a continuous bed of soft flower pops panned left and right, snow sizzle, whooshes as the grass springs up, swallow chirps and wing flutters.

shots.name: 6 Thaw Line
shots.camera: Continuous with shot 5. The FPV dips to 0.4 m and follows the S-curves of a frozen creek that runs down the axis of the lobe. The camera slips about 10 m ahead of the wave, so for a moment we are back in winter. A slight yaw shows the crack running beside us.
shots.content: THE SURPRISE. Milky white ice seals the creek. Just ahead of us a crack zips down the ice faster than we fly, and the plates part into open dark-blue water. That open water reflects a deep-cyan summer sky with towering white cumulus, while the real sky overhead is still flat lavender overcast: the stream already shows a season that has not arrived. Meltwater drips send rings across the reflection, and frosted reeds tick past the frame edges. At 11.6s the front catches up from behind and colour floods the banks again. BUILD: the water shader evaluates the analytic sky function with the spring sky parameters along its reflection vector, so no planar reflection pass is needed. Ripples come from an analytic ring buffer of impacts.
shots.sound: Water gurgles under the ice. A sharp zipper crack runs away ahead of us, followed by shifting plates, tinkles and drip plinks into open water. The music thins to strings and celesta for a beat of wonder (9.8-11.4s), then the percussion rebuilds from 11.6s.

shots.name: 7 Overtaken
shots.camera: Continuous FPV. The camera climbs to 2.5 m and slows from 30 to 20 m/s, so the front overtakes it and passes under the lens. It tilts up gently at 12.2s to catch the sun breaking through, then levels out. At 14.2s a swift crosses 0.3 m from the lens in 3 motion-blurred frames.
shots.content: The wave passes us and the frame flips to full spring. At 12.2s the overcast tears open around the sun: a big warm flare, god rays slanting through drifting pollen, deep cyan sky showing through the tear. Below is a dense, backlit wildflower meadow of translucent chartreuse grass and glowing petals, rolling under wind gusts. Dew sparkles, and petals and pollen stream toward the lens while swallows wheel overhead. The swift near-miss lands at 14.2s. Ahead, a grove of round, snow-laden fluffy trees stands on a low rise.
shots.sound: The music lifts, with the melody in the strings and flute runs over the ostinato. A big airy pass-by whoosh as the front goes under us, a shimmer swell as the sun breaks, a rising dawn chorus of birdsong, meadow wind gusts, and at 14.2s a close swift whoosh-by from left to right with a chirp.

shots.name: 8 Canopy
shots.camera: Pull-up. The FPV climbs steeply (pitch +25 degrees) up the face of the grove and skims 1 m over the crowns at about 18 m/s. From 16.30 to 16.60s it punches through a falling cloud of shed snow that whites out the frame. A hidden cut and a turn of about 160 degrees happen inside the white-out.
shots.content: The fluffy leaf-card crowns are capped with snow. As the wave reaches them they flush from frosted white to fresh lime green, bottom up, and shrug off their snow in big soft puffs that blow into the lens. The backlit leaves glow chartreuse, then the frame whites out. This replaces the original bare forest, so no branch modelling is needed.
shots.sound: A surge of leaf rustle and three heavy, soft 'whumph' snow slides at 15.9s, 16.1s and 16.35s, then a muffled hit on the lens at the white-out. The drums drop out and a riser swells into the reveal.

shots.name: 9 The Basin
shots.camera: The camera emerges from the white-out already turned around, looking back across the basin toward the north rim with the sun behind and to the right. It cranes up from 25 m to 220 m above the grove while gliding forward at about 15 m/s, pitching from 0 to -12 degrees and yawing slowly 10 degrees to the left. 24 mm with a subtle dolly-zoom (field of view narrows from about 55 to 45 degrees during the rise) so the far rim swells.
shots.content: THE REVEAL: a vast round mountain basin about 3 km across, ringed by snowy peaks. The bloom spreads out from the little knoll where the first flower opened, in six lobes of violet and gold racing along the meltwater swales. The front sweeps north across the basin floor, accelerating to about 250 m/s on the time remap. The round lake beside the knoll breaks into drifting, sparkling ice plates and thaws to turquoise. River ice breaks up in a chain. Forest belts on the slopes flush from white to green in rolling waves, and flocks of birds lift off. The overcast dissolves into deep cyan sky, and cumulus towers boil up behind the peaks (BUILD: animated coverage threshold on layered painterly clouds). The far rim is still in winter: a 150 m frozen waterfall hangs there as a pale blue ice curtain. Strong warm side light, layered aerial haze, cloud shadows sliding across the floor.
shots.sound: The big lift: horns and a soaring string melody over a choir pad. Distant lake ice breaks up with deep groans, booming cracks and tinkling cascades. River rush rises, flock wingbeats sound in the distance, over a bed of wind and birdsong.

shots.name: 10 Unbound
shots.camera: Cut. 50-85 mm telephoto from about 600-700 m away, with a slow 3% push-in and a slight tilt up to follow the spray plume. The sun is behind the camera at about 20-25 degrees elevation. Place the camera so the mist plume at the base sits on the 42-degree cone around the anti-solar point and the bow crosses the plume. Verify this on a 1080p still first.
shots.content: SECOND HIT at 20.80s: the front reaches the north rim. The waterfall's ice curtain cracks from top to bottom and shatters, and the freed water thunders 150 m down, throwing up a sunlit spray plume. From 21.4s to 22.4s a vivid primary rainbow draws itself through the mist, then a fainter, reversed secondary bow appears outside it with the darker Alexander's band between them. The cliffs beside the falls flush with moss and hanging flowers, and swifts cut across the plume. BUILD: the waterfall is a curved sheet with scrolling streak noise, foam at the lip, and mist sprites rendered into their own density target. The rainbow is analytic: 42-degree and 51-degree bands multiplied by mist density, composited after Kuwahara. The falls are only ever seen from a distance, so the water can stay painterly.
shots.sound: HIT: a huge ice-curtain shatter layered with a sub impact, and timpani and cymbals swell to their peak. The waterfall roar ramps in with spray hiss. As the rainbow draws at 21.4s, a shimmering sustained string chord with glassy sparkle, then swift calls.

shots.name: 11 The Valley Is a Flower
shots.camera: Cut. High aerial about 1,300 m above the basin floor, south of centre, looking north. It starts at pitch -45 degrees, framed on the knoll through gaps in a scattered cumulus layer below the camera. From 23.8s to 26.5s it rises to about 1,900 m, pulls back and tilts up to about -20 degrees (ease-out) as the clouds slide to the edges of the frame. From 26.5s to 29.0s it holds almost still, drifting 1%, in a majestic hold. 24 mm. Fade to black from 29.0s to 30.0s.
shots.content: The clouds part, and at 25.5s the last cloud shadow slides off the floor and the pattern resolves. The bloom has painted the whole basin into one colossal six-petalled violet flower, the same flower as the opening. Six lobes of violet and cobalt flowers run along the swales, each with its creek as a midvein, outlined in white daisies around a heart of gold buttercups at the knoll. The flower sits in emerald meadow speckled with poppy red-orange. The turquoise river winds between two petals to the lake beside the heart and leaves to the south like a stem. The lower half of the frame holds the flower, foreshortened into an ellipse. The upper part holds forest belts, the glowing plume of the distant waterfall, snowy peaks, and towering sunlit cumulus with lavender shadows under a thin band of deep cyan sky. Sun shafts slant through the cloud gaps across the haze, and pollen and sparkles rise. At 27.5s a tiny violet-gold glint winks at the heart: the first bloom. From 28.0s to 29.0s a few out-of-focus violet petals drift up past the lens. BUILD: at this distance the flower is carried by the terrain albedo colour wash baked from the petal map, with instances faded out, so it reads without dense geometry.
shots.sound: The music resolves: a full major chord lands at 25.50s (choir, strings, horns) and sustains. At 27.5s the opening celesta motif returns as a bookend, with a faint chime on the glint at the heart. It rings out to silence at 30.0s. Under it: wide high-altitude air, the distant waterfall, birdsong, and a soft petal flutter at 28.0s.

palette:
ACT I, FROST (0-6.0s): blue-hour indigo sky #262B55, lavender haze #8F87C4, snow in periwinkle shadow #A9B4E0, rime highlights #E8F1FF, and one thin dawn-gold slot #FFC873 on the horizon. The only chroma is deep violet #4B2A9E between the frosted tepals; the gold light seam appears at 5.2s.
HERO FLOWER (pasque flower): violet #7B4FD6, backlit tepal glow #B48CFF, silver hairs #E6E9F5, gold stamens and pollen #FFC42E. Keep the violet blue-leaning and never let it drift toward pink or magenta (the reference has a hot-pink tree).
ACT II, CHASE (7.6-12.2s): pale lavender overcast #C9C3E6 and glittering snow ahead, saturated spring behind. The creek reflection is the film's first deep cyan #1E8FD8, with white cumulus.
ACT III, SPRING (12.2-30s): sky from deep cyan #1E8FD8 at the zenith to pale cyan #BFE9F5 at the horizon. Cumulus warm white #FFF8EC with lavender shadows #B9B2E0. Grass emerald #2FA35A, backlit chartreuse #A8DC4A, forest viridian #1F6B45. Flowers: poppy red-orange #F2552C (flower heads only, never foliage), buttercup gold #FFD23A, cobalt #2C5BD8, violet #7B4FD6, daisy white #F7F5EE. Water turquoise #36C2C9 with white-gold glitter #FFF1C2. Snowy peaks blue-white #DDE8F7, aerial haze #9CC7E8, sunlight #FFE3A0. The rainbow is the only full-spectrum element.
GRADE: cool shadows and warm highlights. Lift the blacks to blue in Act I instead of crushing them. Saturation rises with the bloom mask and peaks at the rainbow (21-23s) and the flower reveal (25.5s); keep it rich, not neon, and soft-clip chroma on violet and cobalt so they never clip out of gamut. Filmic tonemap (AgX or ACES-like), float16 pipeline, blue-noise dither and fine grain.
hero_moments:
1) 5.20-6.00s HELD BREATH, then 6.00s FIRST BLOOM: silence and frozen time, a gold seam glowing inside the frosted bud, then the six violet tepals snap open on the downbeat and fling off dew. A ring of gold light races out across the snow.
2) 9.8-11.6s THE WRONG REFLECTION (grafted from #1 and #3): the frozen creek zips open just ahead of the wave, and the open water reflects a deep-cyan summer sky with cumulus while the real sky is still lavender overcast. The stream shows the season before it arrives. This is the 'wait, what?' beat, and it costs almost nothing (an analytic sky in the reflection vector).
3) 12.2s OVERTAKEN: the wavefront passes under the lens and the sun tears through the overcast at the same instant, flipping the frame from winter to full backlit spring.
4) 14.2s SWIFT NEAR-MISS: a swift passes 0.3 m from the lens, a whoosh moment for the sound designer.
5) 16.3-16.6s SNOW-PUFF WIPE: the canopy flushes green and sheds its snow into the lens, and the camera comes out of the white-out facing the vast basin as the wave sweeps across it (lake and river ice breaking, forests greening, flocks lifting).
6) 20.8s UNBOUND, then 21.4s DOUBLE RAINBOW (grafted from #4 and #6): the frozen waterfall shatters on the second hit and its spray draws a physically placed 42/51-degree double rainbow with Alexander's dark band. This is the most saturated moment of the film.
7) 25.5s THE VALLEY IS A FLOWER (poster frame, a scale echo grafted from #2): the clouds part from high above and the bloom pattern across the entire basin resolves into the same six-petalled violet flower that opened at 6s, with gold heart, creek midveins, daisy outline and the river as its stem. At 27.5s a tiny glint winks at the heart (the first bloom) on the return of the celesta motif.
WHY IT BEATS THE ORIGINAL BRIEF: a natural fast-marching wavefront (grafted from #5) that races down swales and splits into lobes instead of a perfect radial ring, a mid-film surprise (the reflection), a full-spectrum peak (the rainbow), and a final frame people will replay to catch: the first flower and the last are the same flower. It keeps #0's feasibility because every graft reads from the same baked fields and one wave clock.
music_brief:
MOOD ARC: hushed and crystalline, then a suspended breath, an exhilarating bloom, a wonder beat, a soaring reveal, a triumphant release, and a warm, majestic resolution that ends on the opening motif. The register is Joe Hisaishi (Nausicaa, Mononoke) crossed with RADWIMPS' orchestral 'Your Name' cues: emotional, bright, tasteful, never trailer-bombastic.
INSTRUMENTATION: celesta or glass harmonica and felt piano with high string harmonics for the frost. Spiccato string ostinato, light pulse percussion and flute runs for the chase. Horns, a soaring string melody and a wordless choir 'ah' for the reveal. Timpani and suspended cymbal for the hits. Warm full orchestra and choir for the resolve. Tempo about 96-112 BPM from 6s on; rubato or free time before it.
MANDATORY SYNC POINTS:
- 0.5s: first sustained tone.
- 3.0s: 3-4 note celesta motif.
- 5.20s: hard drop to silence; this must be a true silence, built in the edit if the track doesn't have one.
- 6.00s: MAIN HIT, a full tutti downbeat with low impact.
- 7.6s: ostinato in.
- 9.8-11.4s: thin out to strings and celesta (the wonder beat).
- 11.6s: percussion rebuilds.
- 12.2s: lift as the sun breaks.
- 15.4-16.6s: drums out, riser.
- 16.6s: big melodic swell, the reveal.
- 20.80s: SECOND HIT, the peak (timpani and cymbal).
- 21.4s: shimmering sustained chord for the rainbow.
- 23.8s: begin the descent to the resolve.
- 25.50s: FINAL RESOLUTION CHORD, the flower reveal.
- 27.5s: the opening celesta motif returns.
- 30.0s: ring-out to silence.
LICENSING AND EDIT NOTES: search libraries for a 30s cutdown of 'magical / wonder / uplifting orchestral', ideally a version with a built-in stop before a downbeat. Put every picture event (shot boundaries, wave clock T(t), the creek crack, the sun break, the shatter, the cloud parting, the glint) in one timeline.json. After the track is chosen, snap those times to its real downbeats (up to plus or minus 0.4s) BEFORE the final 4K render, so the picture locks to the music without recutting rendered frames.

risks:
BASE CHOICE: #0 FIRST BLOOM is the base because it is the only concept that both judges rate highly feasible (8 and 8) and that delivers the daylight, saturated, dense-vegetation look in every shot after 7s. #2 scored higher on ideas but depends on an unproven venation prototype. Its strongest asset, the scale-echo hidden pattern, is grafted here cheaply as the valley-flower reveal.
BUILD BACKBONE (the build-order part of these notes):
- Spline-first world: author the shot 11 camera and the master camera splines first, then build the world around them.
- Terrain: a 4x4 km heightfield (fBm plus ridged noise) forming a round basin about 3 km across, with six shallow radial swales from the central knoll, creeks along the swale axes, a river spline, a lake disc and a 150 m north-rim cliff for the waterfall.
- Bake once on the CPU and cache to disk: (a) a petal map (lobes, daisy outline, gold heart, inter-lobe meadow); (b) an arrival-time field from fast-marching or Dijkstra on a 1024x1024 grid seeded at the knoll, with speed raised along the swales and creeks and lowered on spurs and uphill.
- One wave clock T(t), remapped per shot, so that bloomMask = smoothstep(T - arrival(xz)) drives everything: snow layer, grass scale, flower opening, canopy flush, ice break, the sky-clearing direction and particle emitters.
- Instances are generated from GPU hash seeds per terrain chunk, only within about 300 m of the camera. Far away, colour comes from terrain albedo washes.
- Post order: scene pass, then anisotropic Kuwahara, then composite sparkles, pollen, glints and the rainbow, then bloom, god rays/shafts, DOF, grade, dither and grain.
LOOK-DEV ORDER (stills at 1080p, approve before any 4K render): (1) the shot 11 poster still; (2) the hero bud macro; (3) a wavefront frame from shot 5; (4) the shot 10 rainbow geometry; (5) the creek reflection.
RISKS AND MITIGATIONS:
1) The valley flower must read at 25.5s and not look like a crop circle. Make the lobes 250 m or more wide with strong value contrast (violet against emerald), and paint the daisy outline 15-25 m wide in the albedo. Hold the camera at 1,700 m or higher with the flower in the lower half of the frame, keep the lobe edges soft and terrain-following, and use the cloud-parting to stage the reveal. Fallback: if it doesn't read on the still, soften it to an implied pattern. The shot still works as a glorious valley.
2) The hero macro flower could look like CG. Budget the most look-dev here: a subdivided parametric tepal, fuzz, wrap and transmission lighting, rime needle cards, creamy DOF bokeh. If needed, hide the 10-frame burst with motion blur from sub-frames.
3) Every material needs a winter look and a spring look. Use one shared bloomMask/snowLayer function in every shader so each look is tuned once.
4) Grass shimmer and moire at 4K in the FPV shots: 4-8 jittered sub-frames on shots 5-8 only, a minimum blade width in pixels, and distance LOD.
5) Water quality: no close-up water anywhere. The creek is narrow and reflects the analytic sky. The waterfall is seen only from 600 m or more as a streak-noise sheet with mist sprites.
6) Rainbow placement: fix the sun direction and solve the shot 10 camera so the plume sits on the 42-degree cone. Verify on a still.
7) The wrong reflection must read in about 1.5s: keep the overcast very flat and pale, make the reflected sky clearly saturated with bold cumulus shapes, and add a slight yaw so the eye catches it.
8) Banding in the blue-hour gradients and soft sky: float16 targets throughout, blue-noise dither and grain, lifted blacks.
9) Sync with licensed music: drive all timings from timeline.json and retime to the chosen track before the final render.
10) Distance from the references: no ruins, columns or arches. The hero is a small violet wildflower, never a tree, and never pink. The only creatures are swallows and swifts at bird scale. Red-orange appears only as flower heads in green, never as autumn foliage or ferns.
MACHINE SAFETY (required by the user's warning; this laptop is shared with Blender jobs):
- Run exactly one headless Chrome process at below-normal priority, rendering strictly one frame at a time. No parallel workers.
- Never touch, throttle or kill Blender processes.
- Before every batch, check free RAM and whether Blender is rendering or GPU load is high. Pause and wait if free RAM is low (for example under 4-6 GB) or Blender is busy.
- Split Kuwahara, cloud, shaft and rainbow passes into scissor tiles with gl.finish between them, so no single GPU submission comes near the 2-second Windows TDR watchdog. A driver reset could also kill the user's Blender GPU jobs.
- Cap GPU and instance memory at about 1.5-2 GB of the 780M's shared RAM. Reuse render targets and dispose of geometry between shots.
- Bake the fields once and cache them. Do look-dev at 1080p or half resolution.
- Write each frame to disk as soon as it finishes, so the render can resume, and free it.
- Render in batches of about 50-100 frames with cool-down pauses.
- Estimate: about 4-10s per 4K frame, and about 20-40s per frame on the sub-frame shots 5-8. That is roughly 3-4 hours in total for 720 frames at 24 fps, plus pauses.
